# RedRouter: Image Generation

Requires `RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL` and, when the instance requires one, `RED_ROUTER_API_KEY`. See
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/reddb-io/red-router/main/skills/red-router/SKILL.md for setup.

## Discover

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RED_ROUTER_API_KEY" $RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/images/generations
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RED_ROUTER_API_KEY" $RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/models \
  | jq '.data[] | select(.type=="image") | .id'
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RED_ROUTER_API_KEY" "$RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/models/info?id=<model-id>"
```

`GET /v1/images/generations` lists the image models this key can use. `/v1/models/info` shows the
parameters a specific model accepts.

## Endpoint

`POST $RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/images/generations`

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | yes | `provider/model` id, or a combo name |
| `prompt` | usually | image description; a few edit-style models take an image instead |
| `n` | no | image count, provider dependent |
| `size` | no | for example `1024x1024` |
| `quality` | no | provider dependent |
| `response_format` | no | `url` or `b64_json` |

Extra OpenAI-style fields are accepted and passed to providers that understand them. Providers
differ in which fields they honor, so check `/v1/models/info` first.

Related endpoints: `POST /v1/images/edits` (edit an existing image) and
`POST /v1/images/upscale` (super-resolution).

## Example

```bash
curl -X POST $RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/images/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RED_ROUTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"<model-id>","prompt":"watercolor mountains at sunrise","size":"1024x1024","response_format":"b64_json"}' \
  | jq -r '.data[0].b64_json' | base64 -d > out.png
```

JS (URL response):

```js
const r = await fetch(`${process.env.RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL}/v1/images/generations`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RED_ROUTER_API_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: "<model-id>", prompt: "neon city", response_format: "url" }),
});
const { data } = await r.json();
console.log(data[0].url ?? data[0].b64_json?.slice(0, 40));
```

## Response shape

```json
{ "created": 1735000000, "data": [{ "url": "https://..." }] }
```

With `response_format: "b64_json"` each item carries `b64_json` instead of `url`.
